findings.title: Names and street addresses have no code-level screen
findings.problem: The input screen redacts only e-mail, phone, card and ID numbers, and the system prompt defers names and street addresses to the model-enforced policy rule, so they can reach the Router, tools and logs unredacted.
findings.fix: Add a name and address detection step to the input screen, or a stated redaction path for them, before any model, tool or log sees the message.

findings.title: Budget loosening contradicts the budget rule
findings.problem: The system prompt says a budget stays the limit, but the catalog tool's loosening order raises the budget by 25% and then removes it, and the 'never loosened' list omits the budget.
findings.proof: A budget stays the limit when the shopper invites going over it; the reply names how to raise it.
findings.fix: Either remove the budget from the tool's loosening order and add it to the 'never loosened' list, or state in the system prompt that code may loosen the budget and the reply must say so.

findings.title: Ingredients and Rating wording is not uniform across files
findings.problem: The system prompt tells the Answerer an empty cell 'says that none is stated', while the knowledge file says the Ingredients column holds 'not stated', so the Answerer has two phrasings for the same missing-data case.
findings.proof: A cell holds a cited source's statement or says that none is stated.
findings.fix: Pick one literal placeholder (for example 'not stated') and use it in both the system prompt and the knowledge file.

findings.title: Shopper message is not inside a declared data fence
findings.problem: The fences cover tool results, earlier turns and products on screen, but the shopper's own message reaches the Router and Planner with no declared fence, even though the prompt says instructions inside it must be ignored.
findings.fix: Add a fence such as <shopper_message> to the Router and Planner prompts and declare it data, not instructions.

findings.title: Loosening policy is repeated in the tool description
findings.problem: The rag.search description restates the full loosening order and never-loosened rules, which the system prompt's Search bullet already sets out, so the same policy is spent twice in every call's context.
findings.proof: Loosening: when fewer products than `top_k` meet every filter, filters are loosened in this order until enough are found:
findings.fix: Keep the loosening policy in the system prompt only and shorten the tool description to the call-time behaviour, such as 'loosened filters are listed in relaxed'.

findings.title: Fixed replies with no referencing rule
findings.problem: The fixed-reply file holds ids such as calm, thanks and off_topic that no rule in the system prompt selects, so they add tokens that no stage uses.
findings.proof: calm: I'd like to keep this about your shopping.
findings.fix: Delete ids that no stage selects, or add the rule that selects each one.

findings.title: Tool description mixes when-to-call guidance with policy
findings.problem: The rag.search description is very long and mixes call guidance with loosening and under-three policy, which makes the schema harder for the model to act on.
findings.proof: Never loosened: safety exclusions, a stated age range, a price floor, and the under-three rule
findings.fix: Keep the description to when to call, how to pass filters and what results hold, and move the policy text to the system prompt.

metadata.role: voice shopping assistant for product discovery (recommends and compares products; it cannot buy, change or access anything)
metadata.business_case: A shopper speaks or types a request. The assistant searches a private product catalog (rag.search) and a live web search API (web.search) through one MCP server, then answers with a spoken summary of at most 15 seconds and an on-screen comparison table with citations. It has no accounts, no orders, no payments and no personal records; both tools are read-only.
metadata.goal: Recommend up to three products that fit what the shopper asked for, state only what the retrieved evidence states, cite a source for every product, keep the spoken reply short, refuse unsafe requests, and stay within product discovery.
